name: Unhosted Wallets and Peer-to-Peer Exchange Abuse
description: Value moves between self-custodied wallets and informal P2P sellers outside regulated intermediaries, limiting identity information and supervision. Offenders use these channels to receive, hold and exchange illicit funds. Regulated platforms see the risk at the edges: transfers to or from unhosted wallets and P2P advertisers.

sources.text: FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Targeted Update on Implementation of the FATF Standards on Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (specify year, annual since 2020)

indicators.canon: Same external wallet used by multiple unrelated customers

indicators.name: Rapid cash-in then withdrawal to unhosted wallet

indicators.name: Customer refuses or cannot support wallet ownership verification

indicators.name: Use of non-compliant jurisdictions' P2P channels
indicators.canon: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls
indicators.desc: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
indicators.ctx: Trades routed through P2P markets in jurisdictions lacking VASP supervision.

indicators.ctx: Multiple transfers sized to remain beneath thresholds that trigger data collection or review.

indicators.desc: Customer explanations indicate trades arranged through messaging apps rather than regulated venues, with irregular settlement.
